body:
**Shipping to homes** (Queue #705: ship 27 Nov). A home's internet drops: the router reboots, the Wi-Fi password changes, the ISP is down. In the office lamp-4ace has never been tested without the internet. In a home it will be, the first week.

**What a person should see:**
- The lamp says once, plainly and in its own voice, that it can't reach the internet. The voice is offline, so this needs a short line made in advance, on the lamp.
- It shows it in its light: a calm, distinct look, not an error flash.
- Everything that works without the internet keeps working: light, touch, timers and reminders already set, the body.
- It comes back by itself when the internet does, without a restart. It says so only if someone tried to talk to it meanwhile.

**Build:**
1. **Study each part offline first** (no lamp needed for most): the voice (Gemini, and the backup voice #778), memory, tasks (Harness), news, the updater, the eyes' recognition (local), the policy. Run each with its network cut in a test, and record what it does: errors, retries, restarts. Write it in `lampOS/docs/offline.md`, one row a part.
2. **Fix what breaks or restarts.** No part may crash-loop or fill the log when offline.
3. **The words and the light:** one small part watches reachability (not a ping every second; the existing links' own state where they have one) and publishes `lamp/online` on the bus. The voice and Expression use it.
4. **Show it** on a host test with the network cut, then a minute on a lamp with its Wi-Fi turned off (the first builder).

**Kind:** behind a switch first. Owner: nine.

body:
**Why.** Speed: every builder's gate runs the whole `lamp-voice` suite, and on a loaded host one timed test fails in almost every full run, a different one each time, each passing alone. Each such failure costs a rerun and a paragraph of explanation (the fourth builder's #698 comments of 2026-10-14; the first builder's runs of 2026-10-15). On the office Mac (x86_64, load average 6 to 7 with the other builders' sessions and a podman ARM64 build), serial (`--test-threads=1`), in three full runs:

| Run (2026-10-15) | Failed | Message | Alone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23:40 | `coordinator::tests::endpoint_session::complete_verdict_ends_early_but_resumed_speech_keeps_the_turn` | `physical privacy closed or lost freshness` | 5/5 |
| 00:00 | `coordinator::tests::pilot_faults::ring_fault_during_an_answer_keeps_the_conversation_and_cleans_up` | `service privacy freshness lost before next observation`, peer privacy gap 53261 us | 5/5 |
| 01:09 | `coordinator::tests::pilot_faults::sigterm_while_the_failure_notice_plays_stops_cleanly` | `service privacy freshness lost before next observation`, peer privacy gap 6543 us | 5/5 |

All three are the privacy-freshness bound being missed by a test's real worker processes when the host is slow, not a fault in what each test checks.

**Wanted.** Find the bound these tests rely on (the privacy peer's freshness, `crates/voice/src/transport.rs` and the coordinator's privacy observation), and make the tests deterministic on a loaded host without loosening what production enforces: a test clock, or a test-only freshness bound passed in, or the test's own wait for readiness. Show the three passing in ten full serial runs on the Mac while a podman ARM64 build runs beside them, and the native ARM64 CI green.

**Hand back.** The change and the ten runs. One pull request (`fourth-P1`). After #698.

**Most likely wrong.** That production's bound is right for the lamp under load too: if a test misses it at 53 ms, the lamp at 74 °C with the eyes and the voice may as well. Say so if the numbers suggest it.

body:
The order in which each lampOS builder takes its tasks. Kept by the first builder (the one with lamp-4ace); only it edits this body. Decided by the owner and the first builder on 2026-10-14 (`fifth-P3`), replacing the list in `lampOS/docs/work-split.md`, which keeps the rules, the loops, "What the lamp showed" and the history of finished tasks.

**A builder's next task:** the first issue in its own list below that is open and not `status:taken`. Claim it as `lampOS/docs/joining.md` says ("Tasks as GitHub issues"): add `status:taken`, comment `taken by <name> · session <id> · <lamp or none>`, then read the comments again and release it if the first "taken" comment is not yours. Questions and answers are comments on the task's issue. A proposal is a new issue labelled `proposal` and `builder:<name>`; the first builder answers it in a comment, and no answer means not allowed. A finished task is handed back as one pull request from `<name>/<task>` into `lamp-voice`, not a draft, with its ARM64 run green (joining.md, "One pull request per task", `fifth-P6`, decided 18:33); since 2026-10-15 14:50 the reviewer merges it if it is off unless set (`lampOS/builders/reviewer.md`), and the first builder merges the rest after a minute on lamp-4ace. A merge into `lamp-voice` does not close the issue: close it by hand.

Owner's order of 2026-10-14, 14:00: parts that stand on their own first, the harder ones later. And at 17:22: "reimagine the entire experience. make lamp the most fun creature to interact with": the design is `lampOS/docs/creature.md`; its pieces (#710-#714) come first. Stopping and interruption are tested by the first builder in the evenings.

## Ship V2 to homes by Black Friday, 27 November 2026 (the owner, 2026-10-15 16:13)

"we want to ship by black friday or latest by christmas to user's home." Six weeks. Everything below is for that date; anything not on this list waits until after it.

| Date | What is true |
|---|---|
| 1 Nov | Every piece below is on lamp-4ace and switched on; the evening's whole-lamp run passes. |
| 13 Nov | Feature freeze: only fixes from here. Real people have used lamp-4ace every day for two weeks. |
| 13 Nov | The owner makes the update signing key (`LAMPOS_UPDATE_KEY`, docs/updates.md): "later, when it's closer to shipping" (2026-10-15). Until then updates are tested on the unsigned test channel. |
| 20 Nov | Release candidate, signed and delivered by the update channel to every test lamp. |
| 27 Nov | Ship. |

**Must have:** setup for a home (#806, third), signed updates (#737, second, with the owner's key), the voice never dying (#784, #762, fifth), speed (#799 second, #782 fourth), knowing who it is talking to and when not to answer (#800, #753, #792), privacy (#795, third), head touch (#711), the hello and faces (#759, #775), delegation and its news (#751, #765, #798), the backup voice (#778, sixth), giving way to a hand (#780, #790, fifth), and learning from real people (#803, sixth), and **the first five minutes**: the lamp walks its new person through where to sit, their name and face, voice, touch, privacy and giving way (#841, seventh).

## Every component of the brain first (the owner, 2026-10-15 about 07:00)

"in the mvp, did you build ALL the components of the brain? and now have builders perfect/optimize each of those components?" Not yet. These parts of `lampOS/docs/brain-build.md` are missing, or only watching, on lamp-4ace, and each now has a builder. When every row works with the others, each builder owns a set of components to perfect.

| Component (brain-build step) | On lamp-4ace | Task |
|---|---|---|
| Policy deciding when the lamp speaks first (8) | Watches only; decides nothing | **#752 (second)**: progress news through Jev, acting; then hello |
| Who is talking to the lamp: both microphones and the face (7) | **In place, basic**: in a busy room the room microphone's rise (18 dB or more) with the name counts as a call (`LAMP_ATTENTION=busy-near`); the face turned to the lamp is a sign of its own. (Corrected 08:26: I had written that the microphones were never used together.) | Refinement: #753 (fourth), after #733 |
| A second voice when Gemini is down (11) | Says it cannot hear just now | **#754 (sixth)**: proposal first |
| The privacy switch (9) | **In place for the voice microphone** (the voice reads chip 1 line 9 itself and closes it; corrected 08:41, I had written "read by nothing"). The room microphone (Ears) stays open while muted, and the ring shows nothing | **#755 (third)**: Ears closes too, and the ring shows muted |
| Questions around a task: a yes in two breaths (6) | **Works: 5 of 5** since 07:00 (#736 closed) | — |
| A second agent engine: Codex and the others (8) | Claude Code only; built and green on `second/who-gets-the-work` | **#733 (seventh)**: its pull request |
| What the owner teaches and corrects (8) | Covered in part: "remember …" is kept and told to every session. The Policy does not use it | With #752's follow-up (second) |
| The body at power-up, giving way to a hand (12, safety) | Started by hand | **#702, #703 (fifth)** |
| Recognising who is there, memory for each person (4) | **Built, basic (#759, first)**: "remember my face" works end to end, untried with a real face; the hello by name and the name told to the session are in. lamp-4ace stands sideways to the desk, so no face has come near enough yet | #764 (seventh): each person's memory kept apart |
| Setup, network, reset, operator pages (12) | Not built; setup waits on the owner's choice | #699 (third) for the operator's side; setup stays out until the owner decides |

## The V2 MVP first: wide, then deep (the owner, 2026-10-15 00:37)

"prioritize the tasks for builders with ruthless priority. so we have an end to end experience on lamp first. then we'll optimize each component and edge cases later … wide first. deep later … have all the pieces in place make sure the whole works. then after that, have builders optimize each component."

So until every piece below is on lamp-4ace and works with the others, a builder works only on its MVP tasks. Everything else waits under "After the MVP", even if already taken: pause it, push what you have, and say so on its issue.

**ARM64 runs, since 2026-10-15 15:02** (`af7aed833`): the run starts when your pull request into `lamp-voice` is opened (draft or not) and at each push to it, and a newer push cancels the older run. Pushes to `<name>/*` and `lamp-<name>` start none; rebase onto `lamp-voice` so your branch carries the new workflow. Every push to every branch, with four runners a run, had queued eleven runs behind eight, `lamp-voice`'s own among them. Runs on `lamp-<name>` branches were cancelled at 15:02.

**Never end a turn without a wake-up** (the owner, 2026-10-15 14:21: builders 2, 3 and 4 were found idle). A session that ends its turn sits idle until someone types to it, and waiting for an ARM64 run or a review is not a reason to stop. Before you end any turn, schedule your own check in 10 to 15 minutes, with `/loop` or a cron in your session. That check re-reads this Queue and your issues, then carries on: the next step of your task, or your next task if it waits. If your list has nothing you can do, say so on this issue at once, in one line, and the first builder fills it within the hour.

**Never idle, until V2 is done** (the owner, 2026-10-15 about 06:48: "not just finishing the mvp, but keep building until v2 is done!"). If every MVP task in your list is waiting (on a lamp, a person, the owner's key or a review), take your next task under "After the MVP" and keep going. Say on the waiting issue what it waits on. When an MVP task becomes possible again, it comes first.

| It sees you: turns to your face, hello when you arrive, turns to a call, "what do you see?" | Turning to a face and to a call: on. **The hello was only recording, and in 680 sessions it was never once due**; it is switched to speaking today. Sight was built and kept off by the character line; it is switched on today | first builder: both switched on at the next voice restart and tried with a person this morning |

Fixed this morning: a yes in two breaths (5 of 5, #736), a long result ending the voice (#756), and a full store refusing every task after the sixteenth (`e4ece088f`) | Progress while it works: #751 on the lamp, `tasks/status` not yet seen (second); #752 |
